title: Level 3 Art History — Meanings in Art Works 2025
subject: art-history

questions.text:
Answer ONE question. Select and name TWO art works from your studied area(s) or your own choice. Answer BOTH parts of your chosen question.

You will choose a question that focuses on specific meanings communicated through the features of art works. Explain how the meanings are conveyed through the features of the two named art works, and make clear connections between the meanings and the features of the art works.

Aim for a concise response of no more than 5-6 pages. The quality of your writing is more important than the length of your answer.
questions.markingGuide:
WHAT YOU NEED TO INCLUDE:

For Achievement:
- Examine involves explaining the meanings and how these are conveyed through the features of art works.
- It is the connection between the meanings and how they are conveyed that is the key focus.
- The candidate explains appropriate meanings conveyed through features in two named art works, and indicates some connections between the meanings and how they are conveyed.

For Merit:
- Examine in depth involves providing a coherent and considered explanation of the meanings and how the meanings are conveyed through the features of art works.
- The candidate provides a considered explanation, and makes clear connections between meanings and features.
- A typical coherent response will directly address the selected question with an informed explanatory discussion of appropriate meanings, using relevant art historical terminology.

For Excellence:
- Examine perceptively involves explaining how and why meanings are constructed and conveyed through the features of art works, with reference to relevant contextual factors.
- The candidate uses relevant contextual information to support perceptive explanations.
- Perceptive understanding will be apparent in the candidate's fluent and comprehensive knowledge.
- A typical response will directly address all aspects of the selected question with an in-depth contextualised discussion.
